notes:
- **Alt+Z shows the picker sooner.** Before, A9 Snap read every monitor, waited for the slowest one, then handed the pictures to the picker windows one after the other on its window thread. Now each monitor's picture goes to its picker window the moment it has been read, the other checks (the Always secure lookup, the picker windows) run while the screen is being read, and a big picture is converted on four threads instead of one, so the window thread is free again sooner. On a PC with three monitors (5120 x 1440 and two 1440 x 2560) the picker is on screen after about 125 ms instead of about 205 ms (median, from the hotkey to the first picker window; the slowest 1 in 20 went from about 250 ms to about 145 ms).
- **A slow or stuck Alt+Z now leaves a trace.** Every capture writes one `capture timing:` line to the log with how many milliseconds each step took, from the hotkey to the picker on screen, and whether the PC woke from sleep or was unlocked since the last capture. A capture over 300 ms also writes a `slow capture:` line that names the slowest step, and a picker that has drawn nothing after one second says what it is still waiting for, even if you then press Esc. The lines hold times, picture sizes, screen scales and counts only: never a picture, a window title, an app name or a file name (for Always secure, only `yes` or `no`). They stay in the log on your PC; nothing is sent anywhere. The manual's **If something goes wrong** page has a new section, **Alt+Z is slow to appear, or the screen freezes for a moment**, that says where the log is and what each step is.
- **A second Alt+Z while the picker is opening or open** is settled on the hotkey's own thread without waiting for anything: it starts no work and queues nothing.
